questions.title: Which commodity category will record the largest monthly percentage price increase in the FAO Food Price Index for August 2026?
questions.background: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) publishes a monthly index tracking international prices across major food commodity categories.
questions.resolution_criteria: Resolve to the commodity category with the largest percentage price increase from July to August 2026, as reported in the FAO's September 2026 Food Price Index release. Resolution Date: 2026-09-04 Answer with the category name.
questions.current_reasoning: Strong hard-data reinforcement as of 2026-08-24 with 16 of 21 August trading days (76% of the monthly FAO average) now locked in. On Thursday Aug 20, India's Directorate General of Foreign Trade formally authorized 1 million metric tonnes of duty-free raw sugar imports through Oct 31 (India's first major sugar imports since 2016-18) after domestic prices surged 40% in 10 days—driving ICE NY #11 raw sugar to a fresh 15-month high and London #5 white sugar to a 17-month high. Per Barchart on Monday Aug 24, NY #11 raw sugar closed UP another +0.23%, holding near last week's highs and locking in a massive ~+14-17% month-over-month average surge over July's FAO Sugar Index baseline (~14.7 c/lb). Because FAO's Sugar Index tracks pure international sugar prices while Cereals (heavily diluted by stable rice and export wheat benchmarks) and Vegetable Oils (10-oil basket) are damped composites with no comparable Aug 18-24 global price explosion reported in major feeds, we raise Sugar from 0.68 to 0.78, keeping 0.11 on Cereals, 0.09 on Vegetable Oils, and 0.01 each on Dairy and Meat ahead of the final 5 trading days.

questions.title: Which Southeast Asian country will declare a state of emergency over wildfire haze between September 1 and September 5, 2026?
questions.background: Seasonal wildfire smoke can cross borders in Southeast Asia, creating public-health risks and prompting emergency government responses.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official national government announcements, corroborated by reliable news reporting. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the country whose national authorities announce a formal state of emergency because of wildfire haze between September 1 and September 5, 2026, inclusive. The declaration may cover the entire country or a specific area within it. Air-quality warnings, school closures, or health advisories without a formal emergency declaration do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country’s common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Updated on escalating Aug 20-24 regional haze reporting just one week ahead of the Sept 1-5 resolution window. Malaysia's air-quality crisis worsened sharply: Sarawak closed schools across 8 districts Aug 20-21 (Serian API hit 197 on Aug 23, Kuching 185), national asthma cases surged 259%, unhealthy API readings expanded on Aug 24 to 6 Sarawak districts plus 8 districts across 4 Peninsular states, and Malaysia secured Indonesian airspace clearance for joint cloud seeding ahead of Sept 16 Malaysia Day in Sarawak. Because Malaysia's federal authorities have direct statutory precedent for declaring formal localized states of emergency ('Darurat') over haze (1997, 2005, 2013) and have not yet declared one, we raise Malaysia from 0.41 to 0.44. Meanwhile in Indonesia (trimmed 0.46 -> 0.44), El Nino fires across Kalimantan and southern Sumatra triggered ASMC Alert Level 2 and prompted President Prabowo to deploy 1,500 additional troops on Aug 22, though provincial 'siaga darurat' (West/Central/South Kalimantan) and district 'tanggap darurat' (Pontianak, Palangka Raya, Kotawaringin) are already active without a central national state-of-emergency declaration yet. Singapore holds 0.06 (24-hr PSI reached 98 at 9pm Aug 24 and mosque sermons shortened, but zero historical precedent for formal emergency declarations), with Brunei 0.03 and Thailand 0.02.

local_articles.title: The Aryna Sabalenka slump that seeks a flip at US Open
local_articles.snippet: “No thoughts, no emotions. I just want to quit tennis right now.” — Aryna Sabalenka after the French Open. Not the words you tend to hear from a multiple-time Grand Slam champion. Certainly not from the world No.1 for nearly a hundred weeks running. Emotions often run raw and ragged for the Belarusian soon after defeats in Majors, but these lines at the end of her two most recent Slams sum up the Sabalenka slump. One that she will desperately look to arrest at the season-ending US Open, starting Sunday, as the two-time defending champion. The flag-bearer of consistency on the big stages for the last couple of years — the kind seldom seen in the modern women’s tour — Sabalenka stares at her first Slam-less season since 2022.
